title: Drill Hall lease exploration and single-use items bylaw
subtitle: Also: 2024 asset management plan, reusable containers added to bylaw, property tax program report received.
overview: The committee recommended that Council keep the Drill Hall at 72 Farquhar Street rather than sell it, as staff had advised. It rejected the sale {{vote:m6}} and instead recommended that staff explore a lease with the Guelph Centre for Visual Art, with a window ending June 2025 for the group to secure resources. The recommendation adds conditions on equity and inclusion planning and on following the City's engagement principles. It also directs up to $10,000 from the unspent 2024 Community Investment Strategy account toward a public feasibility study due by December 31, 2024.

The committee also recommended the Single-Use Items By-law, phase 2, with reusable containers added to the March 1, 2025 start date {{vote:m4}}. Staff said they would report back before Council's final vote on whether the container change is workable. It recommended approving the 2024 Asset Management Plan for submission to the province by July 1 {{vote:m1}}, with staff to report back on the timeline to sustainable funding during the 2025 budget confirmation process.

The committee received the Financial Needs-based Property Tax Program report for information. A councillor said a motion to improve communication about tax relief programs is planned. All recommendations go to Council for a final decision at its end-of-month meeting.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff explore a lease with the Guelph Centre for Visual Art until June 2025, with the City keeping ownership, equity and engagement conditions, and a staff report back by the end of Q1 2025 {{vote:m14}}.
The committee did not support declaring the Drill Hall surplus and selling it, as staff had recommended {{vote:m6}}.

The committee recommended allocating up to $10,000 from the unspent 2024 Community Investment Strategy account to the arts group for a formal feasibility study, made public by December 31, 2024 {{vote:m15}}.
The committee recommended approving phase 2 of the strategy and the by-law, including reusable containers, with a March 1, 2025 effective date {{vote:m4}}.
The committee added a direction that the by-law also cover reusable containers, with the same March 1, 2025 effective date as phase 2 {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended approving the plan and baseline levels of service, submitting it to the province by July 1, 2024, and bringing back an updated sustainable-funding projection through the 2025 budget confirmation {{vote:m1}}.
The committee received the Financial Needs-based Property Tax Program report for information {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Asset management: staff said the infrastructure backlog will keep growing until funding reaches required levels, and that the projected year for sustainable funding may change as the 2025 budget is developed. Councillors asked about reaching sustainability sooner, the effect of the mayor's budget cap, and why grants rarely cover renewal. Several criticized provincial funding and requirements.

Single-use items: staff did not recommend fees on cups or bags given the economic climate, and said enforcement would start with education. Councillors raised festivals with large volumes of waste and public health concerns. The reusable-container amendment drew support, while staff cautioned that engagement on it had been limited and said they might need to flag timing problems before Council's final vote.

Drill Hall, staff view: staff said the request for expressions of interest stated no City money was available, but the only remaining proposal depended on City funds. They estimated about $125,000 a year to hold the building, and they said that selling it would remove roughly half of that. Housing and other sensitive uses are not allowed near the rail corridor.

Drill Hall, delegates: delegates described a shared community arts space and a long-standing need for affordable studio space. They argued for a phased approach with volunteer and in-kind work, and said the City's investment should be kept for public benefit. Councillors pressed on funding, anchor tenants, public access, accessibility and equity, and asked for firmer commitments before more City resources are committed.

Drill Hall, councillors: supporters of delaying the sale said the building should stay public and that a year was reasonable. Others wanted clearer limits on City costs and were wary of staff seeking outside funding for a third party. One councillor said selling would align with budget restraint. Some wanted clearer parameters before the end-of-month Council meeting.
